economy.summary: His campaign site says his priorities include growing the economy and ensuring access to good-paying jobs, and it opposes what it calls job-crushing regulations such as the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative.
economy.short: Prioritizes economic growth, good-paying jobs; opposes RGGI regulations.

taxes.summary: His campaign site says he worked to stop proposals to increase taxes on working-class families and notes that he declines his legislative per diem.
taxes.short: Says he stopped tax increases; declines legislative per diem.

abortion.summary: His campaign site identifies him as pro-life; the site does not detail specific abortion policy proposals.
abortion.short: Identifies as pro-life; site does not detail policy.

education.summary: In a 2026 primary voter guide he said "More money does not fix education. More parental involvement does," and called for less teaching to tests and more back-to-basics education. His campaign site also says he supports giving parents more control over their children's education.
education.short: Says parental involvement, not money, fixes education; wants back-to-basics.

energy.summary: Opposes the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative, which his campaign site calls a failed policy that would harm Pennsylvania's economy and jobs.
energy.short: Opposes RGGI, calling it harmful to economy and jobs.

guns.summary: Supports Second Amendment rights and introduced Castle Doctrine self-defense legislation. His campaign site also lists supporting public safety by ensuring police have the tools and training to do their jobs.
guns.short: Supports Second Amendment, Castle Doctrine; backs police tools, training.
